definitions.definition: ISO 639-3 language code for Sentani.
To put (something) down, to rest.
To attach or affix (something) to something else, or in or upon a certain place.

parsedExamples.example: I have set my heart on running the marathon.

examples: I have set my heart on running the marathon.

definitions.definition: To put in a specified condition or state; to cause to be.
To start (a fire).
To cause to stop or stick; to obstruct; to fasten to a spot.

parsedExamples.example: to set a coach in the mud

examples: to set a coach in the mud

definitions.definition: To determine or settle.
To adjust.
To punch (a nail) into wood so that its head is below the surface.
To arrange with dishes and cutlery, to set the table.

parsedExamples.example: Please set the table for our guests.

examples: Please set the table for our guests.

definitions.definition: To introduce or describe.

parsedExamples.example: I’ll tell you what happened, but first let me set the scene.

examples: I’ll tell you what happened, but first let me set the scene.

definitions.definition: To locate (a play, etc.); to assign a backdrop to, geographically or temporally.

parsedExamples.example: He says he will set his next film in France.
Her debut novel is set during the U.S. Civil War.

examples: He says he will set his next film in France.
Her debut novel is set during the U.S. Civil War.

definitions.definition: To compile, to make (a puzzle or challenge).
To prepare (a stage or film set).
To fit (someone) up in a situation.
To arrange (type).

parsedExamples.example: It was a complex page, but he set it quickly.

examples: It was a complex page, but he set it quickly.

definitions.definition: To devise and assign (work) to.

parsedExamples.example: The teacher set her students the task of drawing a foot.

examples: The teacher set her students the task of drawing a foot.

definitions.definition: To direct (the ball) to a teammate for an attack.
To gel; to solidify.

parsedExamples.example: This glue sets in five minutes.
This jelly sets within a few hours when refrigerated.

examples: This glue sets in five minutes.
This jelly sets within a few hours when refrigerated.

definitions.definition: To render stiff or solid; especially, to convert into curd; to curdle.
Of a heavenly body, to disappear below the horizon of a planet, etc, as the latter rotates.

parsedExamples.example: The moon sets at eight o'clock tonight.

examples: The moon sets at eight o'clock tonight.

definitions.definition: To defeat a contract.
To begin to move; to go forth.
To produce after pollination.
To be fixed for growth; to strike root; to begin to germinate or form.
To sit (be in a seated position).

parsedExamples.example: He sets in that chair all day.

examples: He sets in that chair all day.

definitions.definition: To rest or lie somewhere, on something, etc.; to occupy a certain place.
To hunt game with the aid of a setter.
Of a dog, to indicate the position of game.
To apply oneself; to undertake earnestly.
To fit music to words.
To place plants or shoots in the ground; to plant.

parsedExamples.example: to set pear trees in an orchard

examples: to set pear trees in an orchard

definitions.definition: To become fixed or rigid; to be fastened.
To have a certain direction of motion; to flow; to move on; to tend.

parsedExamples.example: The current sets to the north; the tide sets to the windward.

examples: The current sets to the north; the tide sets to the windward.

definitions.definition: To acknowledge a dancing partner by facing them and moving first to one side and then to the other, while they do the opposite.

parsedExamples.example: Set to partners! was the next instruction from the caller.

examples: Set to partners! was the next instruction from the caller.

definitions.definition: To place or fix in a setting.

parsedExamples.example: to set a precious stone in a border of metal

examples: to set a precious stone in a border of metal

definitions.definition: To put in order in a particular manner; to prepare.

parsedExamples.example: to set (that is, to hone) a razor

examples: to set (that is, to hone) a razor

definitions.definition: To extend and bring into position; to spread.

parsedExamples.example: to set the sails of a ship

examples: to set the sails of a ship

definitions.definition: To give a pitch to, as a tune; to start by fixing the keynote.
To reduce from a dislocated or fractured state.
To sit or lie (easily etc.) on the stomach; to be digested in a certain manner.
To lower into place and fix solidly, as the blocks of cut stone in a structure.
To wager in gambling; to risk.
To adorn with something infixed or affixed; to stud; to variegate with objects placed here and there.
To value; to rate; used with at.
To establish as a rule; to furnish; to prescribe; to assign.
To suit; to become.
To cause (a domestic fowl) to sit on eggs to brood.
To arrange the casting of a movie.

parsedExamples.example: Paramount Pictures has set Jennifer Love Hewitt for a movie called Two Can Play This Game.

examples: Paramount Pictures has set Jennifer Love Hewitt for a movie called Two Can Play This Game.

A device for receiving broadcast radio waves (or, more recently, broadcast data); a radio or television.

A bias of mind; an attitude or pattern of behaviour.
A piece placed temporarily upon the head of a pile when the latter cannot otherwise be reached by the weight, or hammer.
The width of the body of a type.
A young oyster when first attached.
Collectively, the crop of young oysters in any locality.

The manner, state, or quality of setting or fitting; fit.

Ready, prepared.

definitions.definition: Intent, determined (to do something).
Prearranged.

parsedExamples.example: a set menu
parsedExamples.translation: a meal that is instituted by a restaurateur for a limited occasion
a required reading for a course in an educational institution

examples: a set menu

definitions.definition: Fixed in one’s opinion.

parsedExamples.example: I’m set against the idea of smacking children to punish them.

examples: I’m set against the idea of smacking children to punish them.

definitions.definition: Fixed in a certain style.
A young plant fit for setting out; a slip; shoot.
A rudimentary fruit.
The setting of the sun or other luminary; the close of the day.
General movement; direction; drift; tendency.
A matching collection of similar things. (Note the similar meaning in Etymology 2, Noun.)
A collection of various objects for a particular purpose.
An object made up of several parts.
A collection of zero or more objects, possibly infinite in size, and disregarding any order or repetition of the objects which may be contained within it.
Set theory.
A group of people, usually meeting socially or connected through some shared interest, activity, attribute, etc.
The scenery for a film or play.

The general locations and area where a movie’s, a film’s, or a video’s scenery is arranged to be filmed also including places for actors, assorted crew, director, producers which are typically not filmed.
The initial or basic formation of dancers.
A group of repetitions of a single exercise performed one after the other without rest.
A complete series of games, forming part of a match.
A complete series of points, forming part of a match.
The act of directing the ball to a teammate for an attack.
A musical performance by a band, disc jockey, etc., consisting of several musical pieces.
A drum kit, a drum set.
A class group in a subject where pupils are divided by ability.
Three of a kind, especially if two cards are in one's hand and the third is on the board. Compare trips (“three of a kind, especially with two cards on the board and one in one's hand”).
